t: That that portion of the first section of the Act entitled “An Act to provide for the conveyance to Pinellas County, State of Florida, of certain public lands herein described”, approved June 17, 1948 (Public Law 666, Eightieth Congress), which describes the lands conveyed by the United States to Pinellas County, Florida, is amended to read as follows: “Lot 1 of section 1, township 33 south, range 15 east; lots 1, 2, 3, and 4 of section 5; lots 1 and 2 of section 6; lots 1, 2, and 3 of section 7; lots 1, 2, 3, and 4 of section 8; lots 1 and 2 of section 9; lot 1 of section 17; and lots 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 of section 18 in township 33 south, range 16 east, together with accretion thereto.”

fable.w: This section only amends the legal description of lands previously conveyed to Pinellas County, Florida. The tempting reading is that mentioning a county, which is a local government, signals outside involvement, but the county is just the recipient of a conveyance. No consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue is provided for any party outside the federal government.
fable.s: which describes the lands conveyed by the United States to Pinellas County, Florida, is amended to read as follows

qwen_block.w: This section amends a previous statute to specify the exact legal description of public lands being conveyed to Pinellas County. It is a property transfer provision and does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or other forms of participation by outside parties in a federal decision-making process.
qwen_block.s: That that portion of the first section of the Act entitled “An Act to provide for the conveyance to Pinellas County, State of Florida, of certain public lands herein described”, approved June 17, 1948 (Public Law 666, Eightieth Congress), which describes the lands conveyed by the United States to Pinellas County, Florida, is amended to read as follows: “Lot 1 of section 1, township 33 south, range 15 east; lots 1, 2, 3, and 4 of section 5; lots 1 and 2 of section 6; lots 1, 2, and 3 of section 7; lots 1, 2, 3, and 4 of section 8; lots 1 and 2 of section 9; lot 1 of section 17; and lots 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 of section 18 in township 33 south, range 16 east, together with accretion thereto.”

opus.w: This section only amends the legal description of public lands that a 1948 Act conveyed to Pinellas County. The county is outside the federal government, but it is only the recipient of the land. It is not consulted and takes no part in any federal decision. No comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue is created.
opus.s: which describes the lands conveyed by the United States to Pinellas County, Florida, is amended to read as follows
opus.b: 1. **Tempting-but-wrong reading:** Pinellas County is a local government, so it counts as a party outside the federal government. Its presence might look like participation. That reading fails because the county does nothing here. The section only amends the legal description of lands Congress already conveyed to the county. There is no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue. The county simply receives the land.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends the legal description of land being conveyed to Pinellas County. It does not require consultation, coordination, or participation by the county or any other outside party in the decision-making process. The conveyance itself is a transfer of property, not a participatory mechanism like a hearing, comment period, or advisory committee.
qwen_chat.s: That that portion of the first section of the Act entitled “An Act to provide for the conveyance to Pinellas County, State of Florida, of certain public lands herein described”, approved June 17, 1948 (Public Law 666, Eightieth Congress), which describes the lands conveyed by the United States to Pinellas County, Florida, is amended to read as follows: “Lot 1 of section 1, township 33 south, range 15 east; lots 1, 2, 3, and 4 of section 5; lots 1 and 2 of section 6; lots 1, 2, and 3 of section 7; lots 1, 2, 3, and 4 of section 8; lots 1 and 2 of section 9; lot 1 of section 17; and lots 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 of section 18 in township 33 south, range 16 east, together with accretion thereto.”
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the land is being conveyed to a county (an outside entity), this involves participation. However, the definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants, and a land conveyance is a transfer of property, not a consultative process or decision-making participation by the outside party. The text describes the legal description of the land, not a process of consultation or coordination with the county before the decision was made.
